title: Projection, pressure correction and saddle-point solvers

items.title: Periodic staggered-grid velocity and pressure spaces
items.statement: On the unit torus and the uniform N^d periodic cell grid, define the real cell-centred mean-zero pressure space, face-centred velocity space, their h^d mass inner products, the forward pressure gradient, backward velocity divergence, and the compatible periodic Laplacian Δ_h=D_hG_h, with a fixed sign and index convention.
items.strategy: State cell and face locations, indexing, all operators and inner products; prove claimed well-definedness locally.

items.title: Symmetric saddle-point system, Schur complement, and block preconditioners
items.statement: For a real finite-dimensional saddle system K=[A B^T; B 0] with SPD A and full-row-rank B, define the positive pressure Schur matrix S=BA^{-1}B^T, its exact block-LU solve, the pressure-mass surrogate γM_Q, and the corresponding block-diagonal symmetric preconditioner, with all hypotheses and pressure gauge stated.
items.strategy: Give the typed matrix inputs and output maps; reuse the published block-LU and symmetric-preconditioning conventions.

items.title: Periodic pressure Laplacian gauge, solvability, and uniform Poincare bound
items.statement: For every N≥2 and fixed d≥1, Δ_h maps mean-zero cell arrays bijectively to themselves, its only kernel on all cell arrays is the constants, every periodic discrete divergence has zero mean, and ||q||_{Q_h}≤√d||G_hq||_{M_h} on mean-zero pressures with h=1/N.
items.strategy: Prove the discrete adjoint identity, characterize the kernel by connectedness, and count coordinate paths for the uniform Poincare estimate.

items.title: Second-order consistency of staggered periodic sampling
items.statement: For smooth periodic vector and scalar fields, face/cell sampling R_h on the unit torus satisfies D_hR_hu=R_h(div u)+O(h^2), A_hR_hu=R_h(−Δu)+O(h^2), and G_hR_hp=R_h(∇p)+O(h^2), uniformly in the corresponding mass norms.
items.strategy: Give the exact face/cell sample maps and derive each centered-difference remainder from Taylor's formula with bounded derivatives.

items.title: Exact Schur solve for a full-row-rank symmetric saddle system
items.statement: If A is SPD and B has full row rank, then S=BA^{-1}B^T is SPD, the matrix [A B^T; B 0] has the published block-LU factorization, and the unique solution of [A B^T; B 0][u;p]=[f;g] is p=S^{-1}(BA^{-1}f-g), u=A^{-1}(f-B^Tp).
items.strategy: Prove Schur positivity from full row rank, instantiate the published block-LU result, and verify both equations by substitution.

items.title: Pressure Schur equivalence from inf-sup, continuity, and stiffness scaling
items.statement: For finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces with an SPD velocity form a, continuity constant C_b, inf-sup constant β>0, and α||v||_V^2≤a(v,v)≤Λ||v||_V^2, the positive pressure Schur form satisfies (β^2/Λ)||q||_Q^2≤(BA^{-1}B^Tq,q)_Q≤(C_b^2/α)||q||_Q^2; hence a scaled pressure mass matrix is spectrally equivalent only with these stated constants.
items.strategy: Identify the Schur quadratic form with the squared dual norm of b(·,q), then apply the stated inf-sup, continuity, and energy equivalence bounds.

items.title: Backward-Euler incremental pressure correction on a periodic staggered grid
items.statement: Given N≥2, d≥1, h=1/N, ν>0, Δt>0, divergence-free u^n, mean-zero p^n, and mean-zero periodic forcing, solve the positive Helmholtz predictor, solve the compatible zero-mean pressure-increment Poisson equation, then correct velocity and update pressure with the stated zero-mode gauge.
items.strategy: Specify inputs, outputs, equations, solve order, gauge, and failure/status behavior; a separate theorem proves the solves well-defined.

items.title: BDF2 standard and rotational incremental pressure-correction variants
items.statement: On the same periodic staggered grid, define the BDF2 predictor and pressure-increment Poisson solve, and give both the standard update p^{n+1}=p^n+φ and the rotational update p^{n+1}=p^n+φ−νD_h	ilde u, including the 2Δt/3 velocity correction and admissible starting data; assert no error rate.
items.strategy: Define both variants exactly, state starting-data and mean-zero conditions, and make no unproved stability or accuracy claim.

items.title: Spectrum of a symmetrically pressure-mass-preconditioned saddle system
items.statement: If the Schur matrix satisfies μ_min M_Q≤S≤μ_max M_Q for positive μ_min,μ_max and the block-diagonal preconditioner is diag(A,γM_Q), then every eigenvalue of its symmetric preconditioning lies in the exact intervals obtained from λ_±(μ)=(1±√(1+4μ))/2 with μ∈[μ_min/γ,μ_max/γ], together with eigenvalue 1 on ker B; this is a spectral bound, not an iteration-count claim.
items.strategy: Use finite-dimensional symmetric spectral decomposition and singular pairs of the pressure-scaled divergence block; derive the two-by-two characteristic polynomial.

items.title: Well-definedness of the periodic pressure-correction solves
items.statement: For admissible data in the backward-Euler and BDF2 algorithms, the velocity predictor matrices are SPD, the divergence right-hand side has zero mean, and the pressure Poisson solve has a unique mean-zero solution; thus both variants return a unique next velocity and a uniquely gauged pressure increment.
items.strategy: Test each predictor against its unknown and use the discrete gradient energy; prove compatibility and uniqueness from the pressure Laplacian lemma.

items.title: Mass-orthogonal periodic discrete Helmholtz projection and exact incompressibility
items.statement: The map P_h=I−G_hΔ_h^{-1}D_h, with Δ_h^{-1} taken on mean-zero cell pressures, is the mass-orthogonal projector onto ker D_h; the corrected velocity in the incremental pressure-correction algorithm is P_h	ilde u and is exactly divergence-free.
items.strategy: Verify range, identity on the kernel, and orthogonality using the discrete adjoint relation.

items.title: Modified velocity-pressure energy identity for periodic pressure correction
items.statement: For the backward-Euler incremental pressure-correction step on the periodic staggered grid, the exact identity is ||u^{n+1}||_M^2−||u^n||_M^2+||\tilde u^{n+1}−u^n||_M^2+2νΔt||\mathcal G_h\tilde u^{n+1}||_M^2+Δt^2(||G_hp^{n+1}||_M^2−||G_hp^n||_M^2)=2Δt(f^{n+1},\tilde u^{n+1})_M.
items.strategy: Test the predictor by 2Δt	ilde u, use the discrete adjoint relation, and combine the projection square identity with the pressure increment.

items.title: First-order velocity accuracy for smooth periodic Stokes data
items.statement: For a smooth mean-zero periodic Stokes solution on the unit torus, central staggered-grid spatial differences and the backward-Euler incremental pressure-correction scheme with u_h^0=P_hR_hu(0) satisfy max_{0≤n≤M}||u_h^n−R_hu(t_n)||_{M_h}≤C_T(h^2+Δt), where C_T is independent of h and Δt and depends on the displayed smoothness bounds, ν, and T; no pressure-error rate is claimed.
items.strategy: Project the sampled Stokes equation, prove second-order spatial consistency by Taylor expansion, and apply the contractive backward-Euler recurrence to the discrete divergence-free velocity.

items.title: Steady MINI Stokes pressure-mass Schur bounds
items.statement: For the P1-bubble/P1 mini element on a bounded connected Lipschitz polygonal/polyhedral domain in d=2,3, the steady Stokes Schur matrix for a_ν(u,v)=2ν(ε(u),ε(v)) obeys (C_FC_div(D))^{-2}/(ν(1+d)) M_Q≤BA_ν^{-1}B^T≤d/ν M_Q, with constants independent of h under the stated shape-regularity assumptions and Countable Choice.
items.strategy: Apply the mini-element Fortin inf-sup bound, the homogeneous Dirichlet strain identity, and the local divergence continuity estimate to the generic Schur theorem.

items.title: MINI Stokes block-preconditioned spectral intervals
items.statement: With the pressure mass preconditioner ν^{-1}M_Q on the same steady mini-element Stokes branch, the symmetric block-preconditioned eigenvalues lie in the exact λ_± intervals corresponding to μ∈[(C_FC_div(D))^{-2}/(1+d),d], with eigenvalue 1 on ker B and no generic iteration-count claim.
items.strategy: Substitute the proved mini-element Schur bounds into the general block spectrum theorem and state the resulting intervals.

title: Projection, pressure correction and saddle-point solvers — Examples

items.title: A Neumann pressure correction can break tangential no-slip
items.statement: On the periodic channel (0,1)×T, a smooth provisional velocity with zero trace can have a Neumann pressure correction whose tangential gradient makes the corrected velocity nonzero at the wall; compute an explicit separated solution and the nonzero trace.
items.strategy: Solve the scalar Neumann Poisson equation exactly for a smooth Fourier mode and evaluate the tangential correction at the wall.

items.title: A collocated central gradient misses an alternating pressure mode
items.statement: For even N, the mean-zero collocated pressure p_j=(-1)^{j_1} has zero centered-difference gradient and therefore lies in the pressure-Poisson kernel; constants are not the full gauge kernel on this collocated grid.
items.strategy: Evaluate the centered difference at every index and verify the checkerboard has zero discrete mean.

items.title: A scalar saddle system has golden-ratio preconditioned eigenvalues
items.statement: For A=[1], B=[1], and M_Q=[1], the saddle matrix and exact pressure-mass block preconditioner give eigenvalues (1±√5)/2; compute the exact block solve and spectrum without inferring a general iteration count.
items.strategy: Verify the 2×2 matrix, its determinant polynomial, the block-LU solve, and the two eigenvalues exactly.

items.title: One staggered Fourier mode is removed exactly by pressure correction
items.statement: For a nonconstant mean-zero cell mode q on the periodic staggered grid, a provisional velocity 	ilde u=G_hq is corrected to zero by the pressure increment φ=q/Δt, illustrating the exact projection and pressure gauge.
items.strategy: Use Δ_hq=D_hG_hq and the unique zero-mean pressure solve, then compute the correction exactly.
